articles.title: God's Wisdom Beyond Understanding
articles.description: Discover how Job's story teaches us to trust God's wisdom even when life doesn't make sense. Learn how faith grows through trials and confidence in God's sovereign plan.
articles.summary: When life falls apart, it is natural to ask God why. This message from the life of Job reminds us that while we may not always receive explanations, we can confidently trust God's wisdom, sovereignty, and eternal purposes.
articles.author: ROLCC Pastoral Team

keyTakeaways.item: God's wisdom is greater than human understanding.
Suffering is not always a sign of God's punishment.
God remains sovereign even in life's hardest moments.
Faith grows when we trust God's character over our questions.
Our ultimate purpose is to glorify God through every season.

quiz.question: What realization did Job express in Job 42:3?
options: He had spoken about things beyond his understanding
He no longer believed God cared
He had spoken about things beyond his understanding
He no longer believed God cared
quiz.explanation: Job humbly acknowledged that God's wisdom exceeded his own understanding.

quiz.question: How did God primarily respond to Job's questions?
options: By revealing His majesty and sovereignty
By revealing His majesty and sovereignty
quiz.explanation: God answered by revealing His greatness rather than explaining every detail.

quiz.question: According to the sermon, what can trials accomplish?
options: They can strengthen faith and reveal God's purposes
They prove God has abandoned us
They can strengthen faith and reveal God's purposes
They prove God has abandoned us
quiz.explanation: The sermon teaches that God uses trials to grow our faith and fulfill His purposes.

quiz.question: Where should believers place their confidence during suffering?
quiz.explanation: True peace comes from trusting God's wisdom rather than relying on our own understanding.

articles.title: How to Stop Stressing and Trust God with Your Problems
articles.description: Learn how trusting God instead of relying on yourself brings peace, courage, and confidence through every challenge. Discover biblical lessons from Gideon and 2 Chronicles 20:15.
articles.summary: Life's challenges often tempt us to carry every burden on our own. This message reminds us that God calls us to trust Him in every battle, exchanging anxiety for faith as we rely on His strength instead of our own.
articles.author: Pr. Benson K Sunny

keyTakeaways.item: The battle ultimately belongs to God.
Self-reliance creates unnecessary anxiety and pride.
God often removes our confidence in human strength so we learn to trust Him.
Remembering God's past faithfulness strengthens future faith.
Faith means obeying God while leaving the results in His hands.

quiz.question: According to 2 Chronicles 20:15, who does the battle belong to?
quiz.explanation: The verse declares that the battle belongs to God.

quiz.question: Why did God reduce Gideon's army?
options: To prevent Israel from taking the credit
To prevent Israel from taking the credit
quiz.explanation: God wanted Israel to recognize that victory came from Him, not their own strength.

quiz.question: What practical habit helps believers remember God's faithfulness?
quiz.explanation: Recording God's answers to prayer builds faith for future challenges.

quiz.question: What does trusting God mean according to the sermon?
options: Doing your part while leaving the outcome to God
Relying only on your own plans
Doing your part while leaving the outcome to God
Relying only on your own plans
quiz.explanation: Biblical trust combines faithful action with complete dependence on God.

articles.title: Romans 8:1-11 — Life in the Spirit
articles.description: A Back to the Bible cell fellowship study on freedom in Christ and life by the Spirit, with reflection questions and a short quiz.
articles.author: ROLCC Fellowship Team

sections.heading: Observe
sections.body: Read Romans 8:1-11 slowly. Notice the contrasts Paul draws: condemnation vs no condemnation, flesh vs Spirit, death vs life and peace.

sections.heading: Interpret
sections.body: Paul teaches that those in Christ are set free from condemnation. The mind set on the Spirit brings life and peace.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Where do you feel condemnation or pressure this week? How might setting your mind on the Spirit change how you respond?

discussionQuestions: What does 'no condemnation' mean for believers in Christ?
How does Paul describe the difference between the flesh and the Spirit?
What is one practical way to 'set the mind on the Spirit' this week?

activities.title: Scripture meditation
activities.body: Rewrite Romans 8:1-2 in your own words and share one sentence with your group.

quiz.question: According to Romans 8:1, there is now no condemnation for those who are…
quiz.explanation: Paul grounds freedom from condemnation in union with Christ.

quiz.question: The mind set on the Spirit is life and…
quiz.explanation: Romans 8:6 contrasts death with life and peace.

quiz.question: Walking according to the Spirit means…
quiz.explanation: Paul calls believers to a Spirit-led way of life.

articles.title: Psalm 23 — The Lord Is My Shepherd
articles.description: A Back to the Bible study on God's care and guidance, with discussion questions for cell fellowship.
articles.author: ROLCC Fellowship Team

sections.heading: Observe
sections.body: Read Psalm 23 aloud. What images does David use to describe God's care?

sections.heading: Interpret
sections.body: David portrays God as a shepherd who provides, guides, protects, and restores.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: What valley are you walking through right now? How can you trust the Shepherd's presence?

discussionQuestions: Which phrase in Psalm 23 speaks most to you today?
How have you experienced God's provision or guidance recently?
